plan.english: Son, give the guest water. Seat the guest at the fire. Do not drive the guest away. He who gives to the guest gives to the gods. When a guest arrives, stand up. Cook for the guest.

title: The Old Man's Words on Speech

plan.english: Son, hear the old one. Then speak a good word. Do not say a lie. A lie does not stand. A word is not work. The heart knows; the voice speaks. Do not say what you do not know. By his own work he is known.
Young one, be at work at dawn. Do your own work. Work nourishes him who is at work. He who sits does not eat. He who ploughs the field eats. Whoever toils becomes rich.
A brother does not kill a brother. The mother nourishes the daughter. The daughter follows the mother. Do not leave your own father. Brothers die, you yourself die. Good fame does not vanish.
Son, the giver of good things is praised. He who does not give is not praised. The guest is the gods'. Death seizes the old one. The guest sits at the fire. Whoever is able, let him give.

title: Counsel on the Guest and the Word

plan.english: Young one, lead the guest to the fire. Nourish the guest. Do not kill the guest. He who listens to a word remembers. A famous name does not vanish. The young one learns from the old one. The old man knows.
He who has died does not see the sun. Whoever lives, let him do the work. Do not be afraid of death. Grief comes to the old one. Illness seizes the old one. Whoever is born, dies.
Son, listen to your own father. Do not strike a brother. Do not speak a lie to your father. The sister follows the brother. Two brothers carry the load. Father and mother nourish the daughter.
Son, a king guards the sheep from the wolf. The king is a giver of good things. The king's name stands. The king does not kill a guest. Fame follows the king's work. The king himself dies.
Son, Mother Earth nourishes the sheep. The year goes; the hill stands. The god sees the lie. Dawn becomes bright. Snow covers the hill. When the sun warms it, it melts.

title: To the Young Man on Old Age

plan.english: When you see the old one, young one, stand up. Listen to the old one: he knows. Youth goes away. The year makes the father old. The young one grows up. He who works becomes strong.

Swift horses draw the chariot. The dog recognises the master. If the guest is thirsty, lead him to the spring. He who is thirsty goes to the spring. The wolf fears the dog. When the heart trembles, the knee trembles.

Giving is praised. What is given is not lost. The giver has imperishable fame. To him who guards cattle, the cattle increase. Do not lead the sheep to the marsh. The master leads the sheep to the hill.
Young one, seek imperishable fame. Fame follows work. Whoever does the work, his name is famous. The god hears you well. Do not seek a lie. Remember the work.
What is it that warms the earth, that dries the wool, that becomes bright at dawn? It is the sun.
Who is she that becomes bright when the earth is getting dark, who does not burn, who is the sister of the sun? She is the moon.
Tell me: what is it at which the guest sits, that burns, that the water kills? It is fire.
What is it in which the fish lives, which the sheep drinks, in which fire vanishes? It is water.
Who is it whom you hear but do not see, who drives the snow? It is the wind.
Who is it that comes from the sky, that covers the earth, that melts when the sun warms him? It is the snow.

title: Riddle of the Wheel of the Sun

plan.english: What is it that looks at the earth, that swift horses draw in the sky? It is the wheel of the sun.
What is it that comes, that goes, that makes the father old, and in which the young one grows? It is the year.
Who is she that is the daughter of Sky? When she comes, the dog wakes up. It is Dawn.
What is it to which the guest, the cattle and the sheep go, and which comes forth from the earth? It is the spring.

The wolf saw a dog and said to him: "Dog, you are full. I am thirsty." The dog said: "Follow me, wolf. The master nourishes me." "Are you free?" "I am not free." "Then, dog, I do not follow you." The free one is thirsty; the full one is not free.

title: The Sheep and the Two Horses

plan.english: The sheep had no wool. She saw two horses. One of the two drew a chariot, one of the two carried a load. The sheep spoke to the two horses: "My heart trembles when I see the master driving horses." The two horses said: "Hear, sheep: our heart trembles when we see this: the master cuts off the wool of the sheep." She heard this and went to the field. He who has heard this is afraid.

A bird was sitting on a hazel. The she-wolf saw her and said to her: "Bird, come down. Your voice is good. Let me listen to your voice." The bird said: "She-wolf, you are saying a lie. I know you. I do not come down." The she-wolf went away. He who listens to the she-wolf's word dies.

The sheatfish was swimming in the water, and the fishes were swimming. The sheatfish said to the fishes: "Who is the master of the water?" The fishes became afraid and said to the sheatfish: "Sheatfish, you are the master of the water." The sheatfish ate up a fish. The great one devours the fishes.

title: The Master, the Sheep and the Wolf

plan.english: The master led the sheep to the field. A sheep went astray. The wolf seized her. Then the master saw him and said to him: "Wolf, let go of her!" "You were not protecting her." Whoever does not guard his own sheep, the wolf eats them.

The wolf clothed himself in a fleece. Then he arrived at the sheep and spoke to them: "Sheep, come to me." The sheep heard the voice and said to him: "Wolf, I recognise you." The wool hides him; the voice points him out.

The ram spoke to the dog: "I carry wool. What do you do?" The dog said: "I do the work of the master. I protect him." The master heard them and said to the two of them: "The work of the ram is great, and the work of the dog is great. You two, do your own work."

A bird sat down at the spring. Then she caught sight of a fish and said to it: "Fish, you swim in the water, and I go up to the sky." The fish said: "Bird, I do not go up, and you do not swim." The sky is for the bird, the water for the fish.

A sheep was drinking water at the spring. Then the wolf came and said to her: "Sheep, you drink my water. Who gave you my water?" The sheep said: "The water is not yours. The spring is the gods'." He seized her. The wolf seeks a sheep and finds a word.
The she-wolf saw a horse and said to him: "What is your name?" The horse said: "My name is on the heel." She looked at the heel. He struck her on the head. Do not look at the heel.

Cattle were drawing a chariot. A mouse was sitting on the wheel. The mouse said: "I carry the chariot, and I lead the cattle." The cattle did not listen to him. The chariot went to the field. He who sits on the wheel does not work, and speaks great speech.

The dog was guarding the sheep. Then the she-wolf came and said to the dog: "Dog, give me a sheep, and I will go away." He said: "I do not give her to you. The sheep are not mine; they are the master's." The she-wolf went away. He who guards does not give a sheep to the wolf.

title: The Old Ram and the Young Ram

plan.english: Two rams stood in the field. One of the two was old, one of the two was young. Then snow came. The young one said: "I am big. I do not fear the snow." The old one said: "I know the snow. My heart trembles." The young one became cold. The young one is big; the old one knows.

title: The Bird, the Snake and the Mouse

plan.english: A bird saw a snake creeping toward a mouse. She said to him: "Mouse, the snake creeps to you. Go away!" The mouse heard her and went away. The snake did not seize the mouse. Whoever hears a good word saves himself.

title: The Sheep and the She-wolf Guard

plan.english: The sheep trembled. They arrived at the she-wolf and said to her: "She-wolf, protect us from the wolves." She said: "I will protect you." Then she ate them up. The wolf does not guard sheep; he eats them.

The old dog seized the she-wolf. She went away. The master struck the old dog. The dog said to the master: "Master, I was young, and I guarded the sheep. Now I am old. Do not strike me." Remember the work of the old ones.
